line_text: G-Good day, sir. I-I hope we have something that might aid your fight against D-D-Deathgaze.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: Standing here I feel no less than the captain himself! Someday, someday... My shop in Archades does well, but not well enough to afford a ship. Still, even being able to travel by airship is a luxury I could only dream of when I lived in Rabanastre.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: Business booms in Archades...I'll get that airship yet! Ah, how the draught of success washes away bitter memories of the past. But this is not always a good thing. Life in the Empire is troubled of late. I find myself missing my time in Dalmasca.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: Did you see it? Deathgaze? Have you ever seen anything more hideous? I'm...I'm so scared I can't even move...

speaker: Traveler
line_text: I never knew there were such horrible creatures in the skies. Maybe I'll rethink buying that airship after all...

speaker: Traveler
line_text: I bought my parents a trip to Rabanastre. I'm hoping to do some shopping, find some things you just can't get back home in Archades.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: Rabanastre was even more lovely than I'd hoped. My parents really seemed to enjoy it, too. We're already planning our next trip together. Hopefully the city won't have changed too much by the time we come back. These days, you never know what might happen...

speaker: Traveler
line_text: My father offered to fight that creature, but... at his age!? His army days are long gone.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: If you hadn't come forward to fight that creature, I think my father really would have tried. He has to realize he isn't a fit young man anymore...

speaker: Energetic Boy; Frightened Child
line_text: My brother's off keeping the peace in Dalmasca. Mum, dad, and me are going to visit him!

speaker: Energetic Boy; Frightened Child
line_text: My brother's off keeping the peace in Dalmasca. He said they've got him busier than ever lately. We may not even be able to see him today.

speaker: Energetic Boy; Frightened Child
line_text: If...if my brother were here, he'd do for that beastie, he would! He'd show him what for!

speaker: Energetic Boy; Frightened Child
line_text: You're as strong as my brother! I hope I get to see him soon...

speaker: Perceptive Boy
line_text: I was enjoying a spot of juice over in the saloon, and the barman was tellin' me all sorts of things. Did you know he used to be a sky pirate? Can you imagine?

speaker: Perceptive Boy
line_text: I was enjoying a spot of juice over in the saloon, and the barman was tellin' me all sorts of things about the last war. Do you think another war'll be startin' soon? To hear him talk about it, it just might...

speaker: Perceptive Boy
line_text: Usually when trouble breaks out on the airship, they look for passengers who might be able to help. Hunters, adventurers...you know. But when they can't find anyone, the barman takes things into his own hands. I'd sure like to see that! But he says it'd be too dangerous.

speaker: Perceptive Boy
line_text: I'd never have thought you'd be able to defeat Deathgaze! The barman's stories about sky pirating were okay, but I wanna hear your stories!

speaker: Roamantics
line_text: Your greatest enemy is your own carelessness. The world teems with trouble. Never know when it might come knockin'.

speaker: Roamantics
line_text: The world teems with trouble. For all we know, even now war rages in some distant land.

speaker: Roamantics
line_text: I look out for myself first, others...never. I'm happy enough to fight, but somethin' like this...you have second thoughts.

speaker: Roamantics
line_text: You held your own back there. Impressive.

speaker: Roamantics
line_text: We travel the world, seeking adventure. That's our leader standing over by the window. Grim, strong...just like an adventurer should be, kupo. He's always helping me out, kupo. I hope I can help, too, when we reach the desert. High adventure on the sands... Gotta pull my own weight!

speaker: Roamantics
line_text: We travel the world, seeking adventure. That's our leader standing over by the window. Grim, strong...just like an adventurer should be, kupo. Before we leave for our next adventure, we're going to raise some money working in Nalbina. The reconstruction pay is good I hear. Kupo.

speaker: Roamantics
line_text: Our leader's going to fight the monster...by himself, kupo! It's too dangerous! You have to stop him!

speaker: Roamantics
line_text: I always thought our leader was the greatest man I'd ever known...until now, kupo. But, uh, let's make that our little secret.

speaker: Roamantics
line_text: Easy to let your guard down aboard these airships. But danger is always lurkin', even here. First rule of adventurin' is to keep your eyes open...

speaker: Roamantics
line_text: Tensions are running high of late. If war breaks out, you can be sure these airships won't be runnin'. I'll take fightin' a hoard of monsters over war any day, you can be sure o' that.

speaker: Roamantics
line_text: So you're an adventurer too, are you? Made nice work o' that monster, I'll say that. You'd make a half decent member of the Roamantics!

speaker: Roamantics
line_text: I hear there's a huge dungeon in Nalbina that hardly anyone makes it out of...in one piece, anyway. Makes the blood run cold, it does.

speaker: Roamantics
line_text: Was in Bhujerba the other day. A lot more tense than I recall it bein'. Must be 'cause o' that Marquis Ondore and his Resistance.

speaker: Roamantics
line_text: Hey, we could use a strong fella like yourself! Whaddaya say? Naw, I'm sure you got your own business to tend to. Seein' you fight like that...got a bit carried away is all.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: This...this isn't good. Urp... I think I'm...airsick... Urp...

speaker: Boonswaggled Bookkeeper
line_text: Of all the days for a monster to attack, why today!? If I make it out of this alive, I ain't never runnin' away from my troubles again, I swears it!

speaker: Machinist
line_text: No interruptions! No interruptions! We're discussing plans for our next airship design. We've just come from an inspection of an airship- yard in Archades, kupo. Should it be of Archadian design, built for speed? Or should we place soundness of build first, as we have in the past? No easy choice, kupo.

speaker: Machinist
line_text: No interruptions! Kupo! We're having a most heated discussion about how our airship design efforts should proceed. The Archadians make advancement after advancement. We cannot let ourselves fall behind, kupo!

speaker: Machinist
line_text: Against monsters, an airship of solid build is probably most important. Sturdy and strong, kupo. Something to consider in our next airship design!

speaker: Machinist
line_text: This has been quite an informative experience, kupo. We've learned much that we can incorporate into our next airship design, oh yes, kupo.

speaker: Clumsy Bangaa
line_text: Get lots of moogles working as airship machinists. I been trying for that myself, but my hands are too big to handle some of the finer parts.

speaker: Clumsy Bangaa
line_text: They're short of hands at the airshipyard in Bhujerba. Said they'd have a position for me. I'm still only an apprentice machinist, with two left thumbs at that, but there's nothing for it but to give it my best!

speaker: Clumsy Bangaa
line_text: Those moogles are still going on about airship design...at a time like this! I've heard of dedication, but isn't this a bit much?

speaker: Clumsy Bangaa
line_text: I may have big, clumsy hands, but that's not going to stop me from making the sturdiest airship the world's ever seen. Practice makes perfect!

speaker: Excited Bangaa
line_text: I ain't never been good with heights. So why is it business always sees me headin' to Bhujerba? The Fates have a sense o' humor, don't they?

speaker: Excited Bangaa
line_text: I ain't never been good with heights. At least I've finally managed to get out of my cabin. Used to be I'd stay locked inside the whole trip.

speaker: Excited Bangaa
line_text: Wasn't sure we were gonna make it. I won't feel safe until I've got two feet planted firmly on the ground.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: You killing time, too? My friend's asleep in his cabin. Can you imagine, wasting time sleeping on a voyage like this?

speaker: Traveler
line_text: My friend fell asleep as soon as we got on board. Said he had to save his energy for after we get to Bhujerba. The last time we came, I think he ended up doing something with a group of the guides there. A little odd, but as long as he enjoys himself...

speaker: Traveler
line_text: That gave me quite a fright. I'd hoped for some excitement, but it seems the saying's true: be careful what you wish for. And would you believe my friend slept through the whole thing? Heavy sleeper's an under- statement!

speaker: Deck Swab
line_text: That had me scared out of my wits, kupo! I still can't find them! One minute it was whoosh, the next it was thwaam! Kupo...kupo!

speaker: Imperial
line_text: You're off to fight that thing? I won't stop you, but turn back if things get rough. No sense throwin' your life away.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: I don't think that poor moogle knows whether he's coming or going. Can't say I blame the fella. Quite an ordeal, this.

speaker: Impudent Boy
line_text: Would you mind not standing so close? I'd rather none of your grime and stench rub off on me, thank you.

speaker: Impudent Boy
line_text: An adventurer, are you? That would explain the smell. What business would a provincial such as yourself have in the capital, anyway?

speaker: Impudent Boy
line_text: Couldn't you kill it any faster? That's what you adventurers are supposed to excel at, isn't it? I would have expected more.

speaker: Imperial
line_text: Have you seen a snotty-nosed brat 'round here? A bad seed is what he is. And the fruit doesn't fall far from the tree, if you gather my meaning.

speaker: Imperial
line_text: Have you seen a snotty-nosed brat 'round here? A bad seed is what he is. It's his kind what make the world the sorry chamber pot it is.

speaker: Imperial
line_text: I've a sword, and I'm as willing as the next man. But I'm not as practiced as I once was. We could really do with a hand!

speaker: Imperial
line_text: I wanted all of the lords and ladies who took shelter in the cabins to know the role you played. Well done!

speaker: Loving Man
line_text: If you don't mind, we're in the middle of something here. / Please look at me! We need to talk about this!

speaker: Loving Man
line_text: Would you mind leaving us alone? I'll be joining the army in a matter of days. I want to make the most of our time together. / Would you please listen to me? Once I'm in the army we won't be able to see each other so easily, and—please look at me! Please!

speaker: Loving Man
line_text: We were just talking about you. She was quite impressed with the way you handled that monster. / She says she thinks you're more attractive than I am. Can you believe it? Is that any way to talk?

speaker: Traveler
line_text: My father's a touch acrophobic. I've tried to get him to go up on deck, but it's no good. Gods forbid he ever needs to do business in Bhujerba!

speaker: Traveler
line_text: My father's a touch acrophobic. I've tried to get him to go up on deck, but I'm not having much luck. But I wouldn't have him any other way. If he hadn't retired from the army because of his fear of heights, he'd be out on the front lines now.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: I don't think this has done much for my father's acrophobia. Hasn't done much for me, either.

speaker: Suspicious Bangaa
line_text: You there, boy! Do somethin' about this beast what's attackin' the ship, would ya? I'm too beautiful to die!

speaker: Traveler
line_text: It's no fair! They won't let me go up and see the Imperials fight!

speaker: Traveler
line_text: He's been huddled like this since Deathgaze attacked. I think he might be hurt.

speaker: Flighty Sky Pirate
line_text: Is this as fast as this ship can go? Of all things, why'd they have to steal my airship!? What was that? Did that cloud just overtake us!?

speaker: Flighty Sky Pirate
line_text: Here I am, off to see if there's truth to these rumors of Reddas's death, and it's taking forever and a day to get there! If this were my ship, I'd have been there and back again by now!

speaker: Flighty Sky Pirate
line_text: If this ship weren't so slow, they wouldn't have to worry about monsters and the like attackin'!

speaker: Flighty Sky Pirate
line_text: Guess these passenger ships aren't all bad. A monster attacks you when you're on your own, then you're in for some trouble.

speaker: Kindly Seeq
line_text: This poor lad here lost his parents in the war. So I'm thinkin' of takin' him home with me to Balfonheim. I'll raise 'im right! (snort)

speaker: Kindly Seeq
line_text: This poor lad here, he lost his parents in the war. Hear there are lots of kids like that in Rabanastre. Gonna raise him in Balfonheim. Good 'n' proper!

speaker: Kindly Seeq
line_text: You saved me and the boy...thanks, lad!

speaker: Pirate's Son
line_text: My father's a pirate in Balfonheim. My mom was worried about us gettin' caught up in trouble there, so we went to live with my grandma. But I wanna be able to help my father someday, so I'm trainin' real hard. If any other pirates attack him, I'll run 'em through! Hrrag!

speaker: Pirate's Son
line_text: My father's a pirate in Balfonheim. My mom was worried about us gettin' caught up in trouble there, so we went to live with my grandma. But my father said Balfonheim's about the safest place to be, these days. So I think we're gonna go back to live there pretty soon.

speaker: Pirate's Son
line_text: I dunno...maybe I'm not cut out to fight pirates.

speaker: Stalwart Sky Pirate; Confused Sky Pirate
line_text: I'd gone home to let my leg recover from an accident a while back. Now that it's better, thought I'd head back to Balfonheim. But the, er, service here on the airships is so nice, I might have to reconsider...

speaker: Stalwart Sky Pirate; Confused Sky Pirate
line_text: Balfonheim sure did change while I was away. Without Reddas to run things, work has fallen off...it's all been down hill.

speaker: Stalwart Sky Pirate; Confused Sky Pirate
line_text: This here soldier talks too fast and fancy to catch a word he's sayin'. Go where? Do what?

speaker: Stalwart Sky Pirate; Confused Sky Pirate
line_text: You ever consider findin' work in Balfonheim? Man who can handle himself like that would go far there.

speaker: Imperial
line_text: Young or old, man or woman, the passengers headin' for Balfonheim have a rough look about 'em. Have to stay on my toes.

speaker: Imperial
line_text: Every now and then we get a rough customer in the lot bound for Balfonheim. Have to stay on my toes.

speaker: Imperial
line_text: Got to get these passengers into their cabins, but it's not goin' as smoothly as I'd hoped!

speaker: Imperial
line_text: When the chips were down, I failed. Had to rely on you to save the lot of us. I've got some serious training to do if I'm to be of any real use.

speaker: Despondent Man
line_text: The chocobo on deck up and flew away! It's not every day you see the flyin' variety. Wish I could fly off when the goin' got rough!

line_text: Deathgaze... I heard it'd been attackin' airships, so I signed on to hunt it. Guess I don't have any choice... / I'm beggin' ya! I'm all bark and no bite! Kill it for me! I don't wanna die!

actor: バトル発生イベント監督
function: 賞金首デスゲイズ襲撃_再び
line_text: I fought Deathgaze once before...ran as far and as fast as my legs would carry me. Not this time, though. This time it's goin' down... / What am I saying? Hot air, all of it! Kill this thing for me, please! I don't wanna die!

trigger: requested by インフォメーション.talk_step03
line_text: No one. Truly. Just a gentleman—and I use the term loosely—who does not know when enough is enough. / Rande Enough is enough? Hah! Will you listen to her? Ann, I tell you, you defy all reason. What sane woman would decline a proposal of marriage from a man of my birth, stature, incomes, and obvious charms? Can your mother really mean all that to you? I've told you a thousand times, you must forget these people back in Old Archades! / Forget my own mother? The mother who raised my sisters single-handedly after my father died in the war? I would never marry a person like you. How many times must I tell you? / Rande You seem to share your sisters' dislike of the noble House Lirschell. But what grudge could you possibly harbor against us? / You and your brothers are among the most vulgar men I've ever met. And I've known many vulgars! Using your father to find out where we work! Speaking of work, I'd better get back to it. If you would kindly take your leave, I've a proper passenger to attend to. / Rande Yes, yes...your passengers... An idea comes to mind. Might I interest you in a game of sorts? / What manner of game? / Rande Last year for your mother's name day you and your sisters each sent her a gift you'd found along the routes you work, yes? / What of it? / Rande This year, I propose that you each gather a flower for your mother, and that this boy here informs each of your sisters of the arrangement. If he can deliver the message to every one of them, my brothers and I will abandon all hope of marriage to you and your sisters. / Absurd! You expect a perfect stranger to willingly go from airship to airship delivering this message of yours!? / Rande She has a point. Six ships, six sisters...quite a lot of work for someone we don't know. Better to forget the whole business. And me? I'll begin making the necessary preparations for our wedding. / I'm sorry you've gotten involved in this, sir... If you do see my sisters on the other airships, perhaps you could show them a letter for me? They're chief stewards, like myself. / Rande I can't remember the last time I had more fun. Already visions of you and your sisters joining the noble House Lirschell fill my mind.

trigger: requested by インフォメーション.talk_step03
line_text: Flowers! What a smashing idea! I'll be sure to find something Mother will like. You've already delivered the letter to my other sisters, haven't you? Well then, you've done it! / Deiman I don't believe this! You really pulled it off! / Pulled it off? What are you talking about, Deiman? / Deiman We had a wager going. If we won, you and your sisters would marry into House Lirschell. If we lost, we'd stop courting you entirely. Everything rested on whether this boy would deliver your sister's letter. Rande said he'd pick someone who didn't spend much time on airships... / How...how horrible! Playing games over something like this! Inconceivable! Well, I suppose you can busy yourself telling your brothers the outcome of your little wager. Hmph! / Deiman Blast it all! / I'm sorry for all the trouble we've put you through, sir. But you really have helped us. Thank you. Thank you so much. How silly of me...I should give you something after all you've done. Here, take this. / Between me and my sisters, we'll give our mother a name day she'll not soon forget. Old Archades or not, nothing's more important than family.

line_text: This door leads to our guest cabins. If you'd like to retire until we reach port, you should find the cabins quite comfortable. Should you wish to use a cabin, speak with the chief steward at the counter to my left. She'll be only too happy to assist you.

speaker: Saloon Steward
line_text: One Rabanastre, comin' right up! Last time I was in Rabanastre, let's see... Right after Princess Ashe was born, musta been. Ninth in the Dalmascan line, and the first girl. The people were overjoyed, that they were. The city bustled with life. Rabanastre's fallen on hard times, but she'll get back that ol' magick of hers, just you watch. / Not too quick, are you, boy? You wouldn't know a joke if it bit you on the tail.

speaker: Saloon Steward
line_text: One Nalbina, comin' right up! Truth be told, I don't have fond memories of that place. I'd just crossed the deserts, not a gil to my name...barely made it there alive. A pretty girl found me, brought a skin of the finest water I'd ever drunk. Like an oasis on my lips, it was. / Not too quick, are you, boy? You wouldn't know a joke if it bit you on the tail.

speaker: Saloon Steward
line_text: One Bhujerba, comin' right up! Not many free cities left these days, but the skycity, she's one of 'em. Sky pirates take to her like ducks to water. Those floatin' islands are home to whole flocks of sky pirates. Used to be I was one of 'em. Ha! So long as we didn't cause no trouble, Marquis Ondore was willin' to look the other way. / Not too quick, are you, boy? You wouldn't know a joke if it bit you on the tail.

speaker: Saloon Steward
line_text: One Archades, comin' up! I didn't make it to Archades till after I hung up my sky pirate's wings. Thought I'd try my hand at earnin' a proper livin'. Before I knew it, I was up to my ears in their precious "knowledge," but I couldn't keep up. That's when the Fates stepped in. Came across a young lady set upon by some street thugs, and gave her a helpin' hand. Turns out her father headed the East Ivalice Company. And that is how you find me so gainfully employed. Heh. I was one of the lucky ones, though. The capital breaks ten times as many as it makes. Leaves 'em with no dreams, no money...and no way home. / Not too quick, are you, boy? You wouldn't know a joke if it bit you on the tail.

speaker: Saloon Steward
line_text: One Balfonheim, comin' up! I'm from Balfonheim, and proud of it. Most like you'd guessed at that already. I'd dreamed of bein' a pirate since I was just a whelp. There are as many kinds of pirate as grains of sand on the beach. The lot in Balfonheim are even- tempered, not given to rash violence. A rough bunch, to be sure, but honest, hard- workin' folk, with small patience for idle hands. / Not too quick, are you, boy? You wouldn't know a joke if it bit you on the tail.

speaker: Saloon Steward
line_text: One Rabanastre, comin' right up! Last time I was in Rabanastre, let's see... Right after Princess Ashe was born, musta been. Different times, those were. Happier times. But Rabanastre's people are hardy, strong. They'll win back their freedom, you watch. And it won't be long now, I reckon. / Not too quick, are you, boy? You wouldn't know a joke if it bit you on the tail.

speaker: Saloon Steward
line_text: One Nalbina, comin' right up! I was at death's door the time I was in Nalbina. Heat of the desert had nearly done for me. The water there was the sweetest I'd ever had. She may be famed for the battle over her fortress two years back, but I'll always remember her as a quiet oasis town. / Not too quick, are you, boy? You wouldn't know a joke if it bit you on the tail.

speaker: Saloon Steward
line_text: One Bhujerba, comin' right up! More sky pirate dens out on those floatin' islands than stars in the sky, but Marquis Ondore was willin' to look the other way. Hearin' he'd left Bhujerba over some illness gave me quite a shock. 'Course that was all a part of his ruse. The fortune he's amassed from the magicite trade has helped him build quite an army, but Archadia isn't like to roll over easy. / Not too quick, are you, boy? You wouldn't know a joke if it bit you on the tail.

speaker: Saloon Steward
line_text: One Archades, comin' up! You might say the capital changed my life. That's where I met the head of the East Ivalice Company's daughter and landed this job. The company head may be an Archadian, but he sets social standing aside when it comes to business. He wants all our passengers treated equal. It's good to know there are people like him who don't let the might of Archadia go to their heads. He's all right by me. Heh. / Not too quick, are you, boy? You wouldn't know a joke if it bit you on the tail.

speaker: Saloon Steward
line_text: One Balfonheim, comin' up! I grew up in Balfonheim, you know. Rough folk there, but loyal and true. Taught me what work was, among a good many other things. Been ages since I was back. Hear that it's been a mite more livable since that pirate Reddas showed up a couple of years ago. Was sorry to learn he passed not long since. It's true that the good die young. Heh. Would've liked to meet him just once. / Not too quick, are you, boy? You wouldn't know a joke if it bit you on the tail.

speaker: Saloon Steward
line_text: Deathgaze, eh? Many a sky pirate's lost an airship to that one. You bring it down, you'll be a hero, boy.

trigger: requested by 客呼び出し.for_rbn, 客呼び出し.for_nal, 客呼び出し.for_byu, 客呼び出し.for_alc, 客呼び出し.for_var
speaker: Saloon Steward
line_text: Well, if you didn't go and bag that Deathgaze. Heh. That's a victory for sky pirates the world over. You oughta be proud. Don't worry, I'll be right here behind my counter to sing your praises to all who'll listen. Heh.

trigger: requested by 客呼び出し.for_rbn, 客呼び出し.for_nal, 客呼び出し.for_byu, 客呼び出し.for_alc, 客呼び出し.for_var
speaker: Imperial
line_text: Deathgaze...it's Deathgaze. We should never have tried to fight it. We ought to have fled while we had the chance. But the skies will never be safe while it lives. We have to kill it...somehow. If I only had the strength!

speaker: Charming Woman
line_text: I'll finish my drink alone, thank you. / I always seem to be running into you. I enjoy these chance meetings.

speaker: Charming Woman
line_text: I'll finish my drink alone, thank you. / I always seem to be running into you. I enjoy these chance meetings. Let's hope the world stays in one piece, so we might meet again someday.

speaker: Charming Woman
line_text: You're an accomplished adventurer...glad to have made your acquaintance.

speaker: Migrant Laborer
line_text: You from Rabanastre? Same here. Work keeps me away more than I'd like. I was away during the war, too. Heard a friend o' mine got driven out of the city. Plan on payin' him a visit soon.

speaker: Migrant Laborer
line_text: Wrapped up a long job what kept me from Rabanastre for many a year. Now I'm finally headin' home. Friend o' mine there says it's not a good time to be in Rabanastre. Bah! I say there's no place like home!

speaker: Migrant Laborer
line_text: Women and children first, boy! You plan on runnin', least wait your turn!

speaker: Migrant Laborer
line_text: Got quite a tale to tell my friend once I'm back, eh? 'Course I'm glad to see you make it through to the end, boy.

speaker: Innocent Girl
line_text: Why isn't the barkeep leaving? Shouldn't he hide in one of the cabins, too? What if something happens to him?

speaker: Traveler
line_text: We should be heading into the cabins like everyone else, but my daughter insists on staying here! This is no time for her stubbornness.

speaker: Traveling Merchant
line_text: Friend o' mine was sent off to Nalbina. A petty offense—ought to have been able to pay a fine and be done with it. Turn of ill luck. Luckily he managed to get out, somehow. Saw him toiling away last time I was passin' through Nalbina. Better 'an rottin' in a dungeon.

speaker: Traveling Merchant
line_text: Friend o' mine's workin' on the reconstruction over at Nalbina. Stonemason, he is. Says they've been workin' especially hard at fixin' up the old fortress. Sounds like trouble must be a-brewin'.

speaker: Traveling Merchant
line_text: Good thing we had a strong lad like you here! Not bad for one...so young.

speaker: Migrant Laborer
line_text: Nalbina may be hot, but heat I can stand, if there's gil to be had. It's this dungeon talk what has me worried. I mean really...dungeons? Who ever heard of a city with dungeons? Straight out of a mummer's farce, that. Hope I don't regret this...

speaker: Migrant Laborer
line_text: They're payin' well enough for laborers in Nalbina, but workin' long side prisoners and the like... Not sure I like the sound o' that.

speaker: Migrant Laborer
line_text: Haaa... Thanks for savin' us, boy. Times like that, a man realizes just how precious life is...especially his own!

speaker: Merchant
line_text: These two claim they'll keep me safe. It's good to have people you can rely on, but I'm not sure I care to have them breathing down my neck.

speaker: Wayward Seeq
line_text: Poor lad won't 'ead into the cabins without 'is mum 'n' dad. Safer for 'im in there, though.

speaker: Bohemian
line_text: Amazing! An adventure straight from the pages of a storybook, happy ending and all!

speaker: Mischievous Boy
line_text: Hehe, that oughta do it... / Y-You shouldn't sneak up on people like that! Th-Those could be anybody's initials!

speaker: Mischievous Boy
line_text: Hehe, that oughta do it... / Y-You shouldn't sneak up on people like that! Th-Those could be anybody's initials!

speaker: Mischievous Boy
line_text: Hehe, that oughta do it... / Hey, leave me alone! This time I was carvin' somethin' about how great that battle of yours was!

speaker: Traveling Merchant
line_text: Balms and tinctures sell good, but not so good as magicks. And them not half as good as magicite! Off to Bhujerba to lay in a supply of the finest magicite I can get my hands on. There's huge gain to be had sellin' the stuff in Archades.

speaker: Traveling Merchant
line_text: The Imperials have been buyin' out supplies quick as they come in. Pay a pretty gil for magicite, that they do. I'm gonna be rich!

speaker: Traveling Merchant
line_text: Tell me, lad, what was it you used most fightin' that Deathgaze? Tinctures and tonics? Magicks? Got to know the hot items to keep in stock.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: My sister and I keep a small villa just outside Bhujerba. We're on our way there now. Haven't been on holiday in ages. It'll do us good!

speaker: Traveler
line_text: My sister and I are on our way to the villa we keep near Bhujerba, though I must confess I'm somewhat worried. You see, we're both from Archadia, and Bhujerba is the heart of the Resistance. Do you think we'll be all right?

speaker: Traveler
line_text: I'd fight that creature myself, if only my sister would let me go. She treats me as though I were still a child!

speaker: Traveler
line_text: I have to admit, my sister was right. I'd never have stood a chance against that beast.

speaker: Storekeeper
line_text: What's happening!? What's going on!? I can't get a straight answer. Is the airship going to crash?

speaker: Traveler
line_text: What's going to happen to us? The stewards are saying to take shelter in the cabins, but will that be enough?

speaker: Troubled Passenger
line_text: Why travel by airship, when we have gate crystals? I hope to find some literature on the subject in Archades.

speaker: Troubled Passenger
line_text: Why travel by airship, when we have gate crystals? Perhaps because they make convenient weapons of war. Have gate crystals ever been used to wage war? I hope to find some literature on the subject in Archades.

speaker: Troubled Passenger
line_text: In any emergency, fear is our greatest foe. Keep a cool head, boy.

speaker: Troubled Passenger
line_text: Natural philosophy is not my field, but I believe this Deathgaze you felled is a particularly vicious specimen of wyrm. You have done us a great service. I thank you for protecting the ship.

speaker: Stately Gentleman
line_text: Reduced to traveling amongst commoners... outrageous! A fool, that machinist. He can't even repair a single airship...what good is he?

speaker: Stately Gentleman
line_text: The military receives new ship after new ship, while ours gathers dust awaiting repairs! I've had my fill of these commoners.

speaker: Stately Gentleman
line_text: All this commotion over a fiend. The tales of these adventurers are true. Savages all. The noble hero remains a subject of myth.

speaker: Man of Renown
line_text: You'd think they'd at least let me have a look out on the deck! My next novel is to be a ripping yarn of sky pirates and high adventure... Such a wasted opportunity. To think, I could be gathering priceless material for my novel even as we speak!

speaker: Pompous Gentleman
line_text: You're an adventurer, aren't you? A fine chance to earn a few gil for yourself, wouldn't you say?

speaker: Lovelorn Seeq
line_text: See that viera just there? A famous dancer, she is. I've been followin' her...her career for some time. Such silken moves! (snort)

speaker: Lovelorn Seeq
line_text: See that viera just there? A famous dancer, she is. Her dances stir such pathos! I'm goin' to keep followin' her...her career. (snort)

speaker: Lovelorn Seeq
line_text: A thick-limbed hume woman is tryin' to get into the cabins ahead of this lovely viera! Such audacity! I can't bear it!

speaker: Lovelorn Seeq
line_text: I knew you'd defeat that Deathgaze! I knew it! Maybe it's time I started followin' you...er, your career! (snort)

speaker: Traveler
line_text: Been out here drinkin' since we left port, still haven't heard a peep o' complaint out of me woman. Those cabins must be seriously comfy.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: Them Imperials have been buyin' up all the supplies they can get their hands on. Made a rich man of me. I've gil to spare for drinks! So far me woman's stayed shut up in that cabin of ours, and her naggin' with her. This is shapin' up to be a fine voyage!

speaker: Traveler
line_text: Me woman was sleepin' sound till this Deathgaze attacked. Now she's wide awake. Worse, she knows I been out here drinkin' the whole time.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: Got separated from me pal. If he's already headed for the cabins, well and good, but what if he hasn't? I ain't hidin' till I know he's safe!

speaker: Traveler
line_text: This is no time to argue about who's first! At this rate, none of us will be safe!

trigger: requested by 姉妹イベント監督.イベント用貴族男配置
speaker: Lirschell
line_text: Ah, you must be the lad Rande mentioned the other day. This is...what, your second airship? I doubt you've the funds to see this through. We're sure to win!

trigger: requested by 姉妹イベント監督.イベント用貴族男配置
speaker: Lirschell
line_text: Ah, the fellow my brother was talking about. You're really making a serious run of this, are you? Four sisters to go, though. You won't last.

trigger: requested by 姉妹イベント監督.イベント用貴族男配置
speaker: Lirschell
line_text: So, it's you. My brothers told me you might be coming. But I'm not worried. Still three entire ships to go...

trigger: requested by 姉妹イベント監督.イベント用貴族男配置
speaker: Lirschell
line_text: Already been to four of her sisters, eh? This isn't how it was supposed to be...

trigger: requested by 姉妹イベント監督.イベント用貴族男配置
speaker: Lirschell
line_text: Y-You!? My brothers told me all about you. You've Deiman's ship left, and no others. Surely, uh, you must be exhausted by now, no? No?

speaker: Troubled Passenger
line_text: You have troubles, friend? I went to Archades chasin' dreams, but all I found was trouble. Finally weren't nothin' left but to run away. Out here though, fresh air in my lungs, sky above my head, my troubles don't seem so bad.

trigger: requested by 客呼び出し.for_rbn_先読み
speaker: Troubled Passenger
line_text: Foul words on the wind of late. Wasn't all that long ago the world seemed a brighter place... Well, standin' here goin' on about it won't solve anything, will it.

trigger: requested by 客呼び出し.for_rbn_先読み
speaker: Troubled Passenger
line_text: A real warrior, are you, boy? You feel the weight o' the world pressin' down on you, you let off some steam, hear?

trigger: requested by 客呼び出し.for_rbn_先読み
speaker: Paranoid Man
line_text: I am not here to enjoy the wind against my face or any such mean pleasure in which these others bask. No, I am here to search the skies! They're out there, yes. Out there, at the edge of vision! Waiting, watching... Had I the funds, I would buy an airship for their study. (sigh)

trigger: requested by 客呼び出し.for_rbn_先読み
speaker: Paranoid Man
line_text: I am a researcher of sorts. Yes, I search the skies for...them. The capital is famous for this, too, yes. I thought I had finally seen one, but no, it was only a small imperial airship. They swarm the skies of late.

trigger: requested by 客呼び出し.for_rbn_先読み
speaker: Paranoid Man
line_text: To see Deathgaze itself! Such a privilege, such an...honor!

trigger: requested by 客呼び出し.for_rbn_先読み
speaker: Traveler
line_text: We heard it would be hot in Dalmasca, so we dressed the part. A little chilly out on deck, though.

trigger: requested by 客呼び出し.for_rbn_先読み
speaker: Traveler
line_text: This Dalmascan clothing is quite comfortable, really. And the colors...so unique! I do hope Dalmasca retains its local flavor.

trigger: requested by 客呼び出し.for_rbn_先読み
speaker: Traveler
line_text: Our family is safe because of you. I can never thank you enough.

trigger: requested by 客呼び出し.for_rbn_先読み
speaker: Imperial
line_text: That little girl just over there's been staring up at the sky for some time. Not doing anything dangerous, mind you, but something's not right.

speaker: Imperial
line_text: That little girl just over there's been staring up at the sky for some time. I've not seen her parents. Not safe, with the world as it is.

trigger: requested by 客呼び出し.for_rbn_先読み
speaker: Imperial
line_text: That little girl was staring up at the sky before the monster attacked, and now she's at it again. Wonder what's going through her head? Maybe thinking back on your heroics, eh? Heh heh.

speaker: Troubled Passenger
line_text: No one ever said it would be easy earnin' a livin', but there are limits to what a man can take... How many times have I left the crews in Nalbina. ...How many times have I gone draggin' myself back. Man can't live without gil in his pocket.

speaker: Troubled Passenger
line_text: I ran away from my job in Nalbina, but I've had some time to think things over, and I've decided to go back. Can't say as I know why, but I heard they've raised the wages for people workin' on rebuildin' the fortress.

speaker: Troubled Passenger
line_text: Thanks for stickin' your neck out for us. If you hadn't been here... Well, I'm just glad you were. Precious few places to hide on an airship!

speaker: Migrant Laborer
line_text: ... / Leave me be! I'm in no mood for talk... Urph! I've a touch of airsickness... Please boy, just leave...me be... Ooorph!

line_text: ... / Leave me be! I'm in no mood for talk... Urph! I've a touch of airsickness... Please boy, just leave...me be... Ooorph!

line_text: ... / Leave me be! I'm in no mood for talk... Urph! I've a touch of airsickness... Please boy, just leave...me be... Ooorph!

speaker: Merchant
line_text: Do you think it's because of the reconstruction in Nalbina? All these seeq and bangaa onboard, I mean. It's not helping me relax, I'll say that.

speaker: Merchant
line_text: I'm sure it's these rumors of war brewing behind it. The soldiers buying up so many supplies, I mean. On the one hand, it's good for business. But even so, I have...mixed feelings.

speaker: Merchant
line_text: I've never done well around bangaa or seeq, but I must admit it felt good having them at hand during the attack. Oh, and of course having you at hand was the most reassuring thing of all!

speaker: Wayward Seeq
line_text: Can't find me friend anywhere. You don't suppose I got on the wrong airship? That'd be a fine how-do-you-do, wouldn't it?

speaker: Wayward Seeq
line_text: I'd swear I bought a ticket to the capital, but here I am headed for Nalbina! How'm I ever goin' to find me friend? Eh?

speaker: Wayward Seeq
line_text: First I get separated from me friend, then a monster attacks the ship...what next? At least you were here, eh? Some fine fightin'!

speaker: Boonswaggled Bookkeeper
line_text: I thought I'd contracted to be a keeper of books, but somehow they changed the agreement...they expected me to do heavy labor at the fortress! I don't know how, but they cheated me. I can't work out under the sun like that...I won't! What was I to do but run and hide?

speaker: Boonswaggled Bookkeeper
line_text: I went to Nalbina to be a keeper of books, not a laborer at the fortress. But they had papers affixed with my seal...they fooled me! I don't care what they're willing to pay, I'll have no part in such work. What was I to do but run and hide?

speaker: Boonswaggled Bookkeeper
line_text: As soon as I saw that Deathgaze appear on the horizon, I made for a good hiding place. I feared for my life!

speaker: Bohemian
line_text: You've heard of Theodora the Highborn, I presume. The epic tale of romance and intrigue set against the backdrop of Nalbina Fortress. To think, I'll soon walk the halls and byways of the novel! I cannot wait!

speaker: Bohemian
line_text: You've heard of Theodora the Highborn, I presume. The epic tale of romance and intrigue set against the backdrop of Nalbina Fortress. The very battles have a romantic quality to them. Do you suppose real battles are like that? No. No, I don't suppose they are.

speaker: Bohemian
line_text: You could be the leading man of a great play yourself. How unexpected...in the nicest of ways.

speaker: Migrant Laborer
line_text: Had the most vivid dream that I was thrown into the dungeons at Nalbina, my body wastin' away to nothin'. Ever since, I've walked the true path, on my mother's soul! Just thinkin' on that dream is enough to keep me honest.

speaker: Migrant Laborer
line_text: Had a dream once that I was thrown into the dungeons at Nalbina. Since then, I've mended my ways and walked the true path. I've even thought of helpin' with the fortress reconstruction. Heard they need more hands if they're to finish. If war breaks out with Rozarria, that fortress could mean the difference between victory and defeat.

speaker: Migrant Laborer
line_text: Look at you, boy! The soldiers wouldn't even go near that beast, but you...you didn't even flinch!

speaker: Deck Swab
line_text: We're the cleaning crew, kupo. Been at this job since we were young, and there ain't no one does it better. Just look at that deck, kupo!

speaker: Deck Swab
line_text: We're the cleaning crew, and there ain't no one does it better, kupo! Nearly met our match the other day, though. One of them battleships was in port, you wouldn't believe the filth, kupo! I could barely bear to look. The dirt...the grime! Kupo...

speaker: Deck Swab
line_text: We'll be working a double shift to clean up after that, kupo. But as long as you're all right, you won't hear me complain!

speaker: Storekeeper
line_text: My wife and son will be meeting me at the aerodrome. Business has kept me from home...too long. It will be good to see them again.

speaker: Storekeeper
line_text: I deal in poultices, medicinal herbs, and the like. There's been a great shortage of late... I fear the world braces for what's to come.

speaker: Storekeeper
line_text: I was afraid I'd never see my family again. Thank you for saving us... Thank you!

speaker: Imperial
line_text: Don't be gettin' too friendly with the fairer members of the crew, boy. Don't want you gettin' in the way of their work.

speaker: Imperial
line_text: Don't be gettin' too friendly with the fairer members of the crew, boy. Courtin' that lovely chief steward... Treatin' the shopkeeper Lidia to tea... What? Me? I never— That is to say— Don't be silly, boy!

speaker: Imperial
line_text: You're rather popular among the ladies in the crew, boy. Small wonder after that spectacle. What...me? Jealous? Go on...

speaker: Machinist
line_text: Kupo... Really nice, eh? Kupo-po... These Archadian models seem quite popular among the passengers. I'll have to look into why in more detail, kupo. Thank you for your time. / Kupo... Nothing special? Really? Most interesting. We can't beat them for speed, but perhaps that's not the only thing that matters... Kupo... I thank you for your time. Kupo!

speaker: Machinist
line_text: Kupo... I hate to admit it, but I think you may be right. Archadia is said to be making strides with their warships as well, kupo... We mustn't be outdone. I thank you for your opinion, good sir! / Kupo... I am relieved to hear you think so. Perhaps Archadian airships are not so highly regarded as I'd feared. Still...they are said to be making strides with their warships, kupo... We mustn't be outdone. I thank you for your opinion, good sir!

speaker: Machinist
line_text: You're quite right. Thanks to your efforts. My thanks...you've saved the ship, kupo! / Indeed. Without your heroic efforts, the ship would have been quite defenseless, kupo. Something must be done! And it falls to us machinists to do it, kupo. Passenger safety must come first!

speaker: Traveler
line_text: You see that moogle walking around? I think he's an important machinist. He was asking me what I thought of the airship. Rather clever, blending in with the passengers to find out what they really think.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: You see that moogle walking around? I think he's an important airship designer from Bhujerba. Archadian airships have taken the lead recently. He must be trying to think of new ways to compete.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: That moogle is single-minded about his work. When the monster attacked, he used it as reason to work out improved airship defenses. Incredible.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: My daughters are women grown now. 'Tis as though I travel with my own sisters! The children grow up so very fast...

speaker: Traveler
line_text: My daughters and I have so looked forward to our trip to Bhujerba together. But this talk of a resistance has me rather worried. Is the city safe, do you think? And if it's not, then what?

speaker: Traveler
line_text: My daughters are safe, and I've your courage to thank. You've done a hero's work, boy.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: I'm happy to travel with my mother, though I hate having to leave my husband alone at home.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: I'm happy to travel with my mother, though I hate having to leave my husband alone at home. His work in the army keeps him quite busy, I'm afraid. Far too busy for a holiday such as this.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: My sister and I are in complete agreement. You're a hero, truly! I wonder if my own husband could have defended us so valiantly.

speaker: Suspicious Bangaa
line_text: Can't find that seeq anywhere! I'll bet the fool got on the wrong airship...bah! All our plannin' for nothin'!

speaker: Suspicious Bangaa
line_text: Can't find that seeq anywhere! I'll bet the fool got on the wrong airship...bah! Coulda sworn he asked for a ticket to the capital...

speaker: Suspicious Bangaa
line_text: Maybe I'll make it to the capital after all. Thanks for that, boy.

speaker: Man of Renown
line_text: Vigil for the Black King, Theodora the Highborn...I grow tired of this historical fare. My next work shall be one of high adventure. But what to write about? Inspiration eludes me. I had hoped a stroll on deck might break the silence of my muse.

speaker: Man of Renown
line_text: The stench of war hangs on the air. How am I to write a heart-pounding tale of high adventure in such conditions?

speaker: Man of Renown
line_text: Inspiring heroics, boy! I've the most brilliant idea for my novel! Yes, my quill is poised to write once more!

speaker: Perceptive Boy
line_text: My father says the airship's bridge is in here. When I'm older, I'm going to have him send me to learn to be a pilot.

speaker: Perceptive Boy
line_text: Have you ever seen an Imperial warship? They're amazing! When I'm older, I'm going to have my father send me to be a military pilot.

speaker: Perceptive Boy
line_text: Being a pilot's all right, but being an adventurer looks like fun, too. When I'm older, I'm going to ask my father to let me be an adventurer!

speaker: Pompous Gentleman
line_text: I wouldn't have thought you rootless adventurers could afford to travel by airship. Always casting about for ways to earn gil.

speaker: Pompous Gentleman
line_text: How can an impoverished adventurer such as yourself afford passage to the capital? Mercenary work pay well, does it?

speaker: Pompous Gentleman
line_text: I hope you'll be well rewarded for killing this Deathgaze. You should receive danger money for such perilous work.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: Bhujerba has a city watch, but they can't begin to compare with Archadia's. I think it's probably the helms. My brother's an Imperial soldier, and someday I'm going to join, too! My parents will be ever so proud!

speaker: Traveler
line_text: I heard that Bhujerba has a city watch and some kinda resistance soldiers, too. Not sure what they're supposed to do. I don't think either of them would stand a chance against an Imperial soldier, though.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: My parents were so happy when my brother became an Imperial soldier. So I wanted to be one, too, when I grow up. Now I'm not so sure, though. What if I went off to war and got killed? That wouldn't make them very happy, not one bit.

speaker: Melancholy Father
line_text: See that boy walking just over there? The very image of my own son. His mother and I have separated, and he lives with her, you see. I imagine he must be nearly as tall as that boy there, now...

speaker: Melancholy Father
line_text: See that boy walking just over there? The very image of my own son. He lives with his mother now, you see. His new father is a soldier, so in times like these he is seldom home. I hope his long absences don't traumatize the poor boy further...

speaker: Melancholy Father
line_text: When that creature landed on the deck, I thought I'd never see my son again... Thank you for saving us. Thank you so much.

speaker: Machinist's Apprentice
line_text: Until recently, I worked in the markets, kupo. But I decided I needed to challenge myself, so I've begun studying airship design.

speaker: Machinist's Apprentice
line_text: I've decided to take up the study of airship design, kupo. Someday I hope to draw up plans for a ship—that's why I'm here, in fact! There's much to learn by observing, kupo. I saw some of the warships stationed near Balfonheim... how different from these leisure craft!

speaker: Machinist's Apprentice
line_text: A terrifying, yet edifying, experience, kupo. I must remember to include defenses against flying beasts when designing my airship.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: As soon as I learned the Gran Kiltias had passed on, I set out for Balfonheim. Plan on crossin' by sea to pay my last respects on Bur-Omisace. It's the least I can do for the man who showed me the Light.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: Nothin' but dark news since the Gran Kiltias passed away. (snort) I'm takin' sea passage from Balfonheim to Bur-Omisace to pray everythin' turns out all right.

speaker: Traveler
line_text: You took down that monster with the skill of a master warrior, m'boy! Faram Himself must walk at your side!

speaker: Traveler
line_text: That man and bangaa are acting rather strangely, don't you think? Pacing the deck like that. I'm sure it's nothing...right?

speaker: Traveler
line_text: That man and bangaa are acting rather strangely, don't you think? Pacing the deck like that. Don't they have anything better to do?

speaker: Traveler
line_text: You're the one who killed that monster, aren't you? I'm sure you're tired of hearing it by now, but thank you!

speaker: Bohemian
line_text: I thought I'd be the first one up on the deck, but when I got here, I found this black chocobo. Where did it come from? Could it be someone's pet?

speaker: Bohemian
line_text: This black chocobo was just standing here when I came up on deck. Aren't black birds supposed to bring bad luck? I don't like this...

speaker: Bohemian
line_text: I know this black chocobo must have fled when Deathgaze attacked, but I didn't see it anywhere inside the ship. And now here it is, strutting around like nothing happened. Something's not quite right, but I can't put my finger on it...

speaker: Machinist
line_text: The machinist guild in Balfonheim sent for me to craft glossair rings for them. This'll be my first time in the city...I'm a bit nervous.

speaker: Machinist
line_text: The machinist guild in Balfonheim sent for me to craft glossair rings for them. Machinists are in high demand these days.

speaker: Machinist
line_text: It's a good thing the glossair rings weren't damaged in the battle. Without those, we'd fall right out of the sky. Nicely done.

speaker: Fine Chocobo
line_text: (It looks at you, fierce determination in its eyes.)

speaker: Fine Chocobo
line_text: (It eyes you warily...)

speaker: Fine Chocobo
line_text: (It looks at you with a glimmer of respect in its eye.)
